([[Silver Spring, Maryland]]) | college = [[Charlotte 49ers men's basketball|Charlotte]] (2000–2001) | draft_year = 2001 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 9 | draft_team = [[Detroit Pistons]] | career_start = 2001 | career_end = 2013 | career_number = 5, 7, 3 | career_position = [[Small forward]] / [[power forward]] | years1 = {{nbay|2001|full=y}} | team1 = [[Detroit Pistons]] | years2 = {{nbay|2002|start}}–{{nbay|2004|end}} | team2 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | years3 = {{nbay|2004|end}} | team3 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years4 = 2005–2006 | team4 = [[Bàsquet Manresa]] | years5 = 2006 | team5 = [[CB Bilbao Berri|Lagun Aro Bilbao]] | years6 = 2006–2007 | team6 = [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro|Scavolini-Gruppo Spar Pesaro]] | years7 = 2007–2008 | team7 = [[Zhejiang Lions|Zhejiang Guangsha Lions]] | years8 = 2008 | team8 = [[Arecibo Captains]] | years9 = 2008 | team9 = [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] | years10 = 2008–2010 | team10 = Zhejiang Guangsha Lions | years11 = 2010–2011 | team11 = [[Shandong Golden Stars]] | years12 = 2011 | team12 = [[Anyang KGC Pro Basketball Club]] | years13 = 2012 | team13 = Zhejiang Guangsha Lions | years14 = 2012 | team14 = [[Barako Bull Energy]] | years15 = 2013 | team15 = [[Petron Blaze Boosters]] | highlights = * [[List of Chinese Basketball Association scoring leaders|CBA scoring champion]] ([[2008–09 CBA season|2009]]) * First-team All-[[Conference USA]] (2001) }} '''Rodney Charles White''' (born June 28, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Born in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]], White played [[college basketball]] for the [[Charlotte 49ers men's basketball|Charlotte 49ers]], earning national freshman of the year honors from [[ESPN]]. He was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the ninth overall pick of the [[2001 NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== === Detroit Pistons (2001–2002) === Despite his lofty 9th overall selection, White quickly fell out of favor with new Pistons coach [[Rick Carlisle]] and played in only 16 games during the 2001–2002 season, averaging 3.5 points in 8.1 minutes. === Denver Nuggets (2002–2005) === Sensing untapped potential in White, then [[Denver Nuggets]] General Manager [[Kiki Vandeweghe]] took a gamble in the 2002 offseason, sending a bounty of two players and a future first-round pick to Detroit in exchange for White.[http://www.upi.com/Sports_News/2002/10/01/Pistons-send-Rodney-White-to-Denver/UPI-13871033492735/ Pistons send Rodney White to Denver] White had an inconsistent and tumultuous tenure in Denver. Flashes of brilliance on the offensive end were overshadowed by lack of defensive commitment, drawing the same ire from coach [[Jeff Bzdelik]] he had received from Carlisle in Detroit. Overall, White averaged 7.7 points over 186 games with the Nuggets. His best output coming as an occasional starter during the hapless 17-win [[2002-03 NBA season|2002–2003]] season, in which he averaged 9 points in 72 games. === Golden State Warriors (2005) === That poor season parlayed into a top pick in the [[2003 NBA Draft|draft]], which the Nuggets used to select [[Carmelo Anthony]]. With a surefire star in Anthony now on board, Vandeweghe was able to concede failure and package White with fellow bust [[Nikoloz Tskitishvili]]. Late in the [[2004-05 NBA season|2004–2005]] season, the pair was dealt to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for [[Eduardo Nájera]], [[Luis Flores (basketball)|Luis Flores]], and a future first-round pick.[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/acquire_tskitishvili_white_022405.html Warriors acquire Rodney White and Nikoloz Tskitishvili from Denver] The pick was later sent to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] as part of the [[Allen Iverson]] trade. White played sparingly in 16 games for the Warriors, averaging 5.1 points in 11.7 minutes. White's final NBA game was played on April 20, 2005, in a 106 – 89 win over the Utah Jazz where White recorded 2 points and 1 rebound. White was released by the Warriors the following summer. === Overseas (2005–2013) === White's career picked up in Europe, but his journeyman tag remained. White first caught on in the [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|Spanish League]] with [[Bàsquet Manresa]], followed by a stint with [[CB Bilbao Berri|Lagun Aro Bilbao]]. He was cut by Bilbao on November 1, 2006. The following month, he joined [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro|Scavolini-Gruppo Spar Pesaro]] in the [[Serie A (basketball)|Italian League]] for the remainder of their season. In November 2007, he joined the [[Chinese Basketball Association|Chinese League]] team [[Zhejiang Lions|Zhejiang Guangsha Lions]]. He next played with the [[Arecibo Captains]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|Puerto Rican League]]. In the summer of 2008, he signed a contract with the [[Euroleague]] power [[Maccabi Tel Aviv (basketball)|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].[http://www.prosportsdaily.com/forums/showthread.php?t=245274 Maccabi Tel Aviv lands Rodney White] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110715123736/http://www.prosportsdaily.com/forums/showthread.php?t=245274 |date=2011-07-15 }} He was cut by Maccabi on December 2, 2008. White later played again for [[Zhejiang Lions|Zhejiang Guangsha lions]] in [[Chinese Basketball Association|China]]. On June 15, 2011, he agreed to sign with the [[Anyang KGC]] basketball team in South Korea.{{Cite web|url=http://sports.media.daum.net/soccer/news/k_league/breaking/view.html?cateid=1171&newsid=20110615213212871&p=jumpball|title = 한국인삼공사행 '특급 외인' 화이트 "V1을 위해"}} In 2012, he was signed as an import for the [[Barako Bull Energy]] in the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] replacing former teammate [[DerMarr Johnson]]. He requested for his release due to family reasons after playing six games for the Energy. In 2013, he was signed by the [[Petron Blaze Boosters]], also in the [[Philippine Basketball Association]], replacing [[Renaldo Balkman]], who had been banned from the league after an altercation with a teammate. White himself was subsequently replaced by [[Henry Sims]].[http://www.philstar.com/sports/2013/04/02/926121/petron-taps-ex-hoya-replace-white Petron taps ex-Hoya to replace White] In his two games
